description: Approximate months when fruiting bodies or lasting brackets may be visible in Britain. Dates are broad field-guide guidance, not current local occurrence forecasts.

sources.title: First Nature — British fungi field guide

agaricus-arvensis.where: Unimproved pasture, meadows and grassy woodland edges, often in rings.

agaricus-campestris.where: Short grass in pasture, meadows and older lawns, sometimes in fairy rings.

agaricus-xanthodermus.where: Gardens, parkland and woodland edges, including disturbed grassy ground.

aleuria-aurantia.where: Bare, compacted soil beside woodland tracks, paths and damp disturbed ground.

amanita-citrina.where: Leaf litter and soil beneath beech, oak or conifer trees.

amanita-fulva.where: Soil beneath birch and other trees, often among moss.

amanita-muscaria.where: On the ground beneath birch, pine or spruce, including heathland with trees.

amanita-pantherina.where: Soil beneath broadleaf trees and conifers; uncommon in many areas.

amanita-phalloides.where: Ground near oak, beech and other mature broadleaf trees, including parkland.

amanita-rubescens.where: Leaf litter beneath beech, oak and conifers in mixed woodland.

amanita-virosa.where: Soil in damp woodland, often alongside birch or spruce; localised.

apioperdon-pyriforme.where: Dense clusters on rotting logs, buried stumps and decaying wood.

armillaria-mellea.where: Around the bases and roots of broadleaf trees, stumps and woody debris.

astraeus-hygrometricus.where: Dry, sandy or acidic ground in open woodland and heathland.

auricularia-auricula-judae.where: Dead or dying elder branches, occasionally other broadleaf wood, especially after rain.

boletus-edulis.where: Soil near mature oak, beech, birch and conifer trees.

calvatia-gigantea.where: Nutrient-rich grassland, pastures, field edges and rough lawns.

cerioporus-squamosus.where: Large brackets on broadleaf tree trunks, fallen logs and cut stumps.

chalciporus-piperatus.where: Ground in conifer woodland, especially near pine and other tree roots.

chlorociboria-aeruginascens.where: Bark-free rotting hardwood; look for blue-green stained timber and tiny cups.

chlorophyllum-rhacodes.where: Leaf litter, woodland margins, shrubs and shaded garden edges.

clathrus-archeri.where: Mulch, leaf litter and rich soil in woodland or gardens; scarce and localised.

clitocybe-nebularis.where: Leaf litter in broadleaf and conifer woodland, often growing in arcs.

coprinellus-disseminatus.where: Very large groups around rotting stumps and buried wood.

coprinellus-micaceus.where: Clusters at the base of trees, on stumps and buried wood in parks or woods.

coprinopsis-atramentaria.where: Clusters by tree bases, buried wood and disturbed grassy verges.

coprinopsis-picacea.where: Leaf litter in mature, especially beech, woodland.

coprinus-comatus.where: Lawns, verges, parkland and open disturbed grass.

cortinarius-violaceus.where: Mossy soil in established woodland, often under birch, beech or conifers; uncommon.

cuphophyllus-pratensis.where: Old, low-nutrient pasture and unimproved grassland.

exidia-glandulosa.where: Dead hardwood branches, especially oak and hazel, conspicuous in wet weather.

fistulina-hepatica.where: Low on oak or sweet chestnut trunks and old stumps.

flammulina-velutipes.where: Clusters on dead or dying broadleaf trunks and stumps, often in colder weather.

fomes-fomentarius.where: Persistent hoof-shaped brackets on birch and beech trunks and standing deadwood.

fomitopsis-betulina.where: Brackets on dead, dying or fallen birch trunks; older brackets can remain visible.

ganoderma-applanatum.where: Large, persistent brackets low on broadleaf trunks and stumps.

geastrum-triplex.where: Leaf litter beneath broadleaf trees or scrub, on woodland paths and edges.

helvella-lacunosa.where: Damp woodland soil and mossy banks alongside paths.

hericium-erinaceus.where: High or low on veteran broadleaf trees, particularly old beech and oak; very rare and protected.

hydnum-repandum.where: Mossy soil and leaf litter under broadleaf or conifer trees.

hygrocybe-chlorophana.where: Old, undisturbed, low-fertility grassland, sometimes churchyards.

hygrocybe-coccinea.where: Unimproved, mossy short turf, old meadows and churchyards.

hygrocybe-conica.where: Short grass, unimproved lawns, heathy grassland and grassy banks.

hypholoma-fasciculare.where: Dense yellow clusters on rotting logs, stumps and buried dead wood.

imleria-badia.where: Mossy woodland ground, especially near pine and spruce; sometimes by old wood.

kuehneromyces-mutabilis.where: Clustered on rotting broadleaf logs, particularly beech.

laccaria-amethystina.where: Leaf litter beneath beech and other trees in damp woodland.

laccaria-laccata.where: Open woodland soil, grassy rides and tree-lined heathland.

lactarius-deliciosus.where: On the soil close to pine trees in pine woods or mixed woodland.

lactarius-torminosus.where: Ground beneath birch, especially mossy or heathy sites.

lactarius-turpis.where: Damp acidic woodland ground beneath birch.

laetiporus-sulphureus.where: Bright overlapping brackets on living or dead oak and other broadleaf trunks.

leccinum-scabrum.where: Ground close to birch, on woodland margins and heath with birch.

leccinum-versipelle.where: Soil under birch, often in mossy woodland or heathland.

lepista-nuda.where: Leaf litter, compost-rich soil and woodland edges, sometimes gardens.

lycoperdon-perlatum.where: Woodland leaf litter and grassy clearings, sometimes on heath.

macrolepiota-procera.where: Rough grassland, open woodland, field margins and grassy rides.

morchella-esculenta.where: Well-drained soil beneath trees, in copses, woodland and hedgerows; uncommon.

mucidula-mucida.where: Pale clusters growing from fallen or standing beech wood, often in damp woods.

mutinus-caninus.where: Damp leafy woodland, rich soil, woodchip and shaded hedgerows.

mycena-galericulata.where: Groups on fallen broadleaf logs and stumps in woodland.

mycena-haematopus.where: Clusters on rotting hardwood, especially fallen beech branches and logs.

neoboletus-luridiformis.where: Acidic soil near oak, beech and conifers in woodland.

phallus-impudicus.where: Leaf litter and rich soil in woods, hedges and scrub.

pholiota-squarrosa.where: Dense scaly clusters at tree bases and around old stumps.

pleurotus-ostreatus.where: Shelves on dead or dying broadleaf trunks, especially beech; often after cool rain.

russula-cyanoxantha.where: Leaf litter and soil in oak and beech woodland.

russula-emetica.where: Mossy, damp acidic ground in conifer woodland and boggy edges.

russula-ochroleuca.where: Acidic woodland soil beneath conifers, oak or beech.

sarcoscypha-austriaca.where: Decaying sticks in damp leaf litter or moss, particularly shaded streamside woods.

scleroderma-citrinum.where: Dry sandy or acidic soil under trees, on paths and heathy ground.

suillellus-luridus.where: Soil beneath mature broadleaf trees, often on calcareous ground.

trametes-versicolor.where: Layered, persistent brackets on dead broadleaf logs, stumps and branches.

tremella-mesenterica.where: Yellow jelly-like folds on dead broadleaf twigs; most visible after wet weather.

xylaria-hypoxylon.where: Small black-and-white antler shapes on rotting hardwood stumps and logs.

xylaria-polymorpha.where: Dark club-shaped growths at the base of broadleaf stumps, often beech.
